title: 93｜为什么我们彻底爱上尼泊尔徒步！（交通住宿背夫花费全盘点）
title_en: 93 | Why We Fell Completely in Love with Trekking in Nepal! (Transport, Lodging, Porters, and Costs — Fully Broken Down)
summary_cn: 前时尚杂志编辑 Sophie 与三三走完全球前十的 ACT（安纳普尔纳环线）精华段后复盘：烂路吉普车、Teahouse 住宿、背夫向导、饮食踩坑、换钱策略、4月完美天气窗口、装备查缺补漏，以及博卡拉/穆克提纳特/加德满都吃喝玩乐——缺点能忍、优点极想回去，给 ACT 打 8.5-9 分
summary_en: Former fashion magazine editor Sophie and host Sansan walked the highlights of the Annapurna Circuit, one of the world's top ten treks, then came back to review everything: the brutal jeep rides, teahouse lodgings, porters and guides, food pitfalls, money-exchange strategy, the perfect April weather window, gear gaps, and how to eat, drink, and play in Pokhara, Muktinath, and Kathmandu. The downsides are tolerable and the upsides make them want to go back — they give the ACT an 8.5 to 9 out of ten.

scenes.title_en: Transport: The Terrible Roads Are the Entry Ticket
scenes.context: 尼泊尔公路极差，城市间靠吉普车；12 小时烂路的体验与包车/拼车的取舍。语域：casual 亲历吐槽 + 攻略。
scenes.speak: Let's start with transport, because the terrible roads are the entry ticket to Nepal. Getting between cities basically means jeeps. Hiring a private jeep costs more, but it's far more comfortable than sharing, and you leave on your own schedule. The key insight: after twelve hours of terrible roads, you open the curtains to see the snow mountains and instantly feel it was worth it. But enduring that road just for a Poon Hill sunrise is terrible value — it only pays off as part of the multi-day ACT trek. A typical scene: a team of four hires a jeep for about 1,000-plus yuan per person, including seats for the porters. As they say, you only really feel how bad the road is after riding it for twelve hours — and the next morning, opening the curtains and seeing the snow mountain made all twelve hours worth it. Funny enough, a shared jeep with seven or eight people is cramped but everyone locks each other in place, so you don't bounce; a private jeep with four people plus two porters is too loose, and everyone bounces around like pinballs. There are no seat belts in the back, so you hold the overhead handle with one hand until it goes stiff after an hour — pick an experienced driver if you can, because the Poon Hill stretch is especially dangerous.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：尼泊尔公路极差，城市间移动基本靠吉普车。包车虽贵但舒适度远超拼车，且可按自己时间出发
sentences.en: Nepal's roads are terrible, so getting between cities basically means jeeps. Hiring a private jeep costs more, but it's far more comfortable than sharing, and you leave on your own schedule.
sentences.note: 表达提示private jeep → 包车；shared jeep → 拼车；on your own schedule → 按自己的时间

sentences.cn: 关键理解：12小时烂路后拉开窗帘见雪山，瞬间觉得值了。但如果只为 Poon Hill 看日出而忍受这段路，性价比很低——必须搭配 ACT 多日徒步才划算
sentences.en: The key insight: after twelve hours of terrible roads, you open the curtains to see the snow mountains and instantly feel it was worth it. But enduring that road just for a Poon Hill sunrise is terrible value — it only pays off as part of the multi-day ACT trek.

sentences.note: 表达提示per person → 人均；porter → 背夫

sentences.note: 表达提示lock each other in place → 互相卡住；bounce around → 颠来颠去；pinball → 弹球

scenes.context: ACT 沿途完全围绕徒步设计的住宿设施与背夫制度。语域：casual 亲历分享 + 费用盘点。
scenes.speak: Next, lodging and porters. The whole ACT route is built around trekkers, so you don't need to carry heavy supplies. At noon there are teahouses for tea and fried noodles; at night you stay in guesthouses, with prices climbing as the altitude does. The best view was the little standalone room in Selikaka, with a floor-to-ceiling window facing the snow mountains, for just 75 yuan a night — as beautiful as Switzerland, no worse than Switzerland. As the episode notes, you don't need to carry tons of supplies or go heavy-weight along the way, because there are lodging options the entire route. Porters cost 20 dollars a day, and a guide doubling as porter costs 25 — after the agency's cut, they take home less than 100 yuan a day. Crossing the 5,400-meter pass in a hoodie and no down jacket, carrying 30 kilos and walking faster than the tourists, without even a sound of heavy breathing, and wearing plain sneakers instead of crampons. As they say, he was the fastest one the whole way — carrying all that weight, he was still way ahead of us, looking totally relaxed. To make it real: book through a proper agency in Kathmandu or Pokhara to avoid fake roadside guides, agree that the price includes meals, and don't take your porter elsewhere to eat on the sly.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：ACT 沿途设施完全围绕徒步设计，不用重装带补给。中午有 T-House 喝茶吃炒面，晚上住 Guest House，价格随海拔升高
sentences.en: The core mechanism: the whole ACT route is built around trekkers, so you don't need to carry heavy supplies. At noon there are teahouses for tea and fried noodles; at night you stay in guesthouses, with prices climbing as the altitude does.
sentences.note: 表达提示teahouse → 茶屋/茶馆；guesthouse → 民宿客栈；altitude → 海拔

sentences.en: The key insight: the best view was the little standalone room in Selikaka, with a floor-to-ceiling window facing the snow mountains, for just 75 yuan a night — 'as beautiful as Switzerland, no worse than Switzerland.'
sentences.note: 表达提示floor-to-ceiling window → 落地窗；standalone room → 独栋房间；as beautiful as → 不输

scenes.title_en: Food: The Global Champion of Bad Taste
scenes.context: ACT 饮食的踩坑——素食、鸡蛋、Dal Bhat 与超贵热水。语域：casual 亲历吐槽 + 攻略建议。
scenes.speak: Now, the food — and brace yourself. Hindu influence makes vegetarian food dominant, so protein basically means eggs — and by the end, the sight of an egg makes you want to throw up. Vegetables are all root vegetables, mainly potatoes, and the chicken doesn't taste like chicken. Yak beef steak and burgers only appear above Manang. As they put it, when it comes to bad food, Nepal takes first place — even worse than Switzerland — and the worst part is you have no options. A typical scene: the Dal Bhat set meal, rice with lentil soup and pickles, refillable, goes from 550 rupees at the bottom to 850 to 1,000 up the mountain. Bottled water is 150 rupees for 1.5 liters — much cheaper than hot water. And the classic pitfall: the night before crossing Thorung La, one pot of hot water cost 120 yuan, about 2,400 rupees — the most expensive hot water in town — and they downed several pots before even looking at the price. To make it real: bring a camping stove to boil water for drinking and washing, pack wet wipes, mouthwash, and floss picks for days you can't properly wash, buy apples at little shops along the way for fiber, and in Manang grab yak salami and apple cider for a treat. And mind the eggs — someone in the group got stomach trouble the day the fried eggs were made with the wrong oil or undercooked.

sentences.cn: 印度教影响素食多，蛋白质基本靠鸡蛋，吃到后面看见鸡蛋就想吐。蔬菜全是根茎类（土豆），鸡肉不像鸡肉。马南以上才有牦牛肉牛排/汉堡
sentences.en: Hindu influence makes vegetarian food dominant, so protein basically means eggs — and by the end, the sight of an egg makes you want to throw up. Vegetables are all root vegetables, mainly potatoes, and the chicken doesn't taste like chicken. Yak beef steak and burgers only appear above Manang.
sentences.note: 表达提示vegetarian → 素食；protein → 蛋白质；root vegetable → 根茎类蔬菜；yak → 牦牛

sentences.cn: （引用）「在难吃这件事情上，我觉得目前尼泊尔排第一，比瑞士还难吃……难吃的点在于你没得可选。」

sentences.en: A typical scene: the Dal Bhat set meal, rice with lentil soup and pickles, refillable, goes from 550 rupees at the bottom to 850 to 1,000 up the mountain. Bottled water is 150 rupees for 1.5 liters — much cheaper than hot water.

sentences.en: The key insight: the night before crossing Thorung La, one pot of hot water cost 120 yuan, about 2,400 rupees — 'the most expensive hot water in town' — and they downed several pots before even looking at the price.
sentences.note: 表达提示Thorung La → 陀龙拉垭口；a pot of hot water → 一壶热水；the most expensive → 最贵的

sentences.cn: （引用）怎么落地：带炉头烧水喝/洗脸；带湿巾、漱口水、牙线棒应对无法洗漱；路过小卖部多买苹果当膳食纤维；马南买牦牛肉萨拉米和苹果酒解馋
sentences.en: How to make it real: bring a camping stove to boil water for drinking and washing; pack wet wipes, mouthwash, and floss picks for days you can't properly wash; buy apples at little shops along the way for fiber; and in Manang, grab yak salami and apple cider for a treat.

sentences.note: 表达提示undercooked → 不够熟；stomach trouble → 肠胃不适

scenes.context: 每人每天 200 人民币的预算经验，以及 ATM 与现金问题。语域：casual 攻略 + 踩坑复盘。
scenes.speak: On money and budget. Following their friend Xiaoxiong's advice, 200 yuan per person per day — covering lodging and food — is mostly enough, but doesn't include shopping or extra items like horse rides. The key insight: Manang is the last stop reachable by car, with an ATM that might be empty; Muktinath, past the pass, also has an ATM. Changing plans mid-trip or riding a horse needs extra cash. As they admit, they changed money based on 200 yuan a day and overspent so much that by the time they reached Muktinath, they were out of cash. There's a budget version — buses, free lodging, and one dish per meal could squeeze it down to 50 yuan a day — but, in their words, they're too old for that kind of suffering.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：按小熊建议每人每天准备200人民币（含住宿+饮食）基本够用，不含购物和骑马等额外支出
sentences.en: The core mechanism: following their friend Xiaoxiong's advice, 200 yuan per person per day — covering lodging and food — is mostly enough, but doesn't include shopping or extra items like horse rides.
sentences.note: 表达提示per person per day → 每人每天；cover → 覆盖；extra expense → 额外支出

sentences.cn: 关键理解：马南是汽车可达最后一站，有ATM但可能没钱；翻过垭口后穆克提纳特也有ATM。临时改行程、骑马需额外准备
sentences.en: The key insight: Manang is the last stop reachable by car, with an ATM that might be empty; Muktinath, past the pass, also has an ATM. Changing plans mid-trip or riding a horse needs extra cash.

scenes.context: 天气决定徒步体验，以及裤装叠穿比羽绒裤更实用的装备心得。语域：casual 经验分享 + 装备建议。
scenes.speak: Then there's weather and gear. March to May is the best trekking season, but this year the rainy season came early. They landed in the window between snowstorms and fog, got clear skies every day, and never once used their rain gear. The key insight: weather decides everything — without good weather it's hard to keep going, especially when summit views are the goal. After a teammate left, they continued on the Mandali Dream route and failed to summit because of thick fog. As they say, without good weather, it's really hard to find the will to keep going. On gear: when your legs feel restricted, climbing gets much harder — layering softshell pants, fleece pants, and leggings is more practical than a down pair. Though colder seasons or long stretches in snow might still call for down pants. Their advice: as long as your upper body has enough warm layers, just wear one pair of pants.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：3-5月是最佳徒步季，但今年雨季提前。她们卡在前后下雪起雾之间，天天大晴天，雨具完全没用上
sentences.en: The core mechanism: March to May is the best trekking season, but this year the rainy season came early. They landed in the window between snowstorms and fog, got clear skies every day, and never once used their rain gear.
sentences.note: 表达提示trekking season → 徒步季；rainy season → 雨季；clear skies → 大晴天；rain gear → 雨具

sentences.cn: 关键理解：天气决定一切——没有好天气很难支撑走下去，尤其冲顶看景色。队友小路走后继续曼达里梦线，因大雾冲顶失败
sentences.en: The key insight: weather decides everything — without good weather it's hard to keep going, especially when summit views are the goal. After a teammate left, they continued on the Mandali Dream route and failed to summit because of thick fog.
sentences.note: 表达提示summit → 冲顶；thick fog → 大雾；keep going → 支撑走下去

sentences.en: Why it matters: when your legs feel restricted, climbing gets much harder — layering softshell pants, fleece pants, and leggings is more practical than a down pair.
sentences.note: 表达提示restricted → 束缚的；softshell pants → 软壳裤；fleece pants → 抓绒裤；down pants → 羽绒裤

phrases: Good weather is the whole game on a trek.

scenes.title_cn: 博卡拉 / 穆克提纳特 / 加德满都
scenes.context: 三座城市的吃喝玩乐与踩坑——费瓦湖、和平塔、108 圣泉与加德满都的灰。语域：casual 游记 + 城市点评。
scenes.speak: Finally, the three cities. In Pokhara: rowing on Phewa Lake, seeing the Shiva temple from the World Peace Pagoda — it looks like a theme park in Avatar colors — and zoning out in lakeside cafés. The tailoring shop was a pitfall: they agreed to pick up clothes on day three and nothing had even been started, and the quality was mediocre. For advanced play, you could learn rock climbing, learn coffee, then take on other routes. Muktinath marks the end of the ACT's highlight section, and many turn back here. Hindu pilgrims bathe at the 108 sacred springs on the hilltop; the Tibetan Buddhist nunnery has almost no visitors, but knocks open its door. Warming your feet at the hotel's fire pit is an unforgettable experience. As they say, when you step into a Tibetan Buddhist temple, you get this very clean, sacred feeling. And then Kathmandu: the moment you step out you're wrapped in dust and noise — narrow streets, too many cars, and motorbikes squeezing together, making any stroll exhausting. So the fix is to shop quickly and leave — don't expect a city experience.

sentences.cn: 费瓦湖划船、世界和平塔看湿婆神庙（像主题公园/阿凡达配色）、湖边咖啡馆发呆。裁缝店「壁垒」踩坑：约定第三天取衣结果完全没开工，衣服质量一般
sentences.en: In Pokhara: rowing on Phewa Lake, seeing the Shiva temple from the World Peace Pagoda — it looks like a theme park in Avatar colors — and zoning out in lakeside cafés. The tailoring shop was a pitfall: they agreed to pick up clothes on day three and nothing had even been started, and the quality was mediocre.
sentences.note: 表达提示World Peace Pagoda → 世界和平塔；theme park → 主题公园；tailoring shop → 裁缝店；mediocre → 质量一般

sentences.cn: （引用）进阶玩法：学攀岩、学咖啡，再走其他线路
sentences.en: Advanced play: learn rock climbing, learn coffee, then take on other routes.
sentences.note: 表达提示rock climbing → 攀岩；advanced play → 进阶玩法；take on → 挑战

sentences.cn: ACT 精华段终点，很多人到此折返。山顶108圣泉印度教徒沐浴朝圣，藏传佛教尼姑庵几乎无游客但敲门即开。酒店火塘烤脚是难忘体验
sentences.en: Muktinath marks the end of the ACT's highlight section, and many turn back here. Hindu pilgrims bathe at the 108 sacred springs on the hilltop; the Tibetan Buddhist nunnery has almost no visitors, but knocks open its door. Warming your feet at the hotel's fire pit is an unforgettable experience.
sentences.note: 表达提示sacred spring → 圣泉；pilgrim → 朝圣者；nunnery → 尼姑庵；fire pit → 火塘

sentences.cn: （引用）「来到藏传佛教寺庙的时候，就会有一种非常干净圣洁的感觉。」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'When you step into a Tibetan Buddhist temple, you get this very clean, sacred feeling.'
sentences.note: 表达提示sacred → 圣洁；clean feeling → 干净的感觉

sentences.cn: 原因：出门即被灰尘和噪音笼罩，街窄车多摩托车挤一起，逛街很累
sentences.en: The reason: the moment you step out you're wrapped in dust and noise — narrow streets, too many cars, and motorbikes squeezing together, making any stroll exhausting.
sentences.note: 表达提示dust and noise → 灰尘与噪音；squeeze together → 挤在一起；exhausting → 累

sentences.cn: 解法：快速采购后离开，不要期待城市体验
sentences.en: The fix: shop quickly and leave — don't expect a city experience.
sentences.note: 表达提示shop quickly → 快速采购；don't expect → 不要期待

paraphrase.intent: 想说「穆克提纳特是折返点」
phrases: Muktinath is where most trekkers turn around.
The highlight run ends there; the rest is optional.
paraphrase.chunks: turn around · the highlight run ends

paraphrase.intent: 想说「加德满都又脏又挤，快速离开」
phrases: Kathmandu is dusty and chaotic — shop and split.
Grab what you need and get out of the city.
paraphrase.chunks: shop and split · grab and get out
paraphrase.usage: 两句同义，适合攻略口吻

practice.cn: 用「worth it」说：看到雪山的瞬间觉得 12 小时烂路值了。
practice.en: The moment I saw the snow peaks, the twelve-hour road felt worth it.

practice.cn: 用「outpace」说：背着 30 公斤的背夫走得比游客还快。
practice.en: Carrying 30 kilos, the porter still outpaced every tourist.

practice.cn: 用「no options」说：尼泊尔食物难吃的点在于没得选。
practice.en: The worst part of the food is that you have no options.

practice.cn: 用「out of cash」说：到穆克提纳特时他们已经没钱了。
practice.en: By the time they reached Muktinath, they were out of cash.

pitfalls.wrong: The road is very bad, my body is shaking.
pitfalls.right: The road was brutal — we bounced around for twelve hours.
pitfalls.why: body is shaking 是中式说法；bounce around / be jolted 更描述乘车颠簸。

pitfalls.wrong: We hired a labor to carry our bags.
pitfalls.right: We hired a porter through a proper agency.
pitfalls.why: 背夫不是笼统的 labor；porter 是专有名词，且强调通过正规渠道预订。

pitfalls.wrong: The food is the most difficult to eat in the world.
pitfalls.right: Nepal wins the crown for the worst food on earth.
pitfalls.why: 「难吃」不是 difficult to eat；win the crown for worst food 是地道吐槽。

pitfalls.wrong: We changed 200 yuan money each person every day.
pitfalls.right: We changed about 200 yuan per person per day.
pitfalls.why: 中式语序；per person per day 是标准表达，money 冗余。

shifts.before: 以为徒步必须重装带补给
shifts.after: ACT 沿路住宿饮食齐全，轻装即可，设施完全围绕徒步设计
75 元的小独栋雪山大落地窗，比五星级更难忘

shifts.before: 以为难吃是没办法的事
shifts.after: 带炉头、湿巾、苹果和小卖部零食，把饮食坑变成可控变量
